title: Tamsin and the Tryouts
premise: Kestrel Crane, a sardonic coder who runs an anonymous account that keeps predicting school events too accurately, is paired by his teacher with Tamsin Vale — his longtime nemesis and the only person who suspects the account is his — for a semester project documenting the school's dying robotics team. Forced to rebuild the team together, Kestrel discovers the 'tryouts' are really about who gets to belong: Tamsin needs the championship to save her scholarship, while Kestrel must pass a final audition for a prestigious coding academy that terrifies him more than any rival. As their found family of misfit teammates grows, Kestrel's account is exposed, nearly destroying everything. In the end he loses the championship that doesn't matter but wins the audition that does — choosing to stay, publicly, as himself.
about_author: Freya Amberdale is a former debate coach who writes stories about sharp-tongued teenagers learning to be soft with each other. She lives in a rainy coastal town with two cats named after failed inventions.

chapters.title: Day One Hundred and Twelve
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. He counts down days to graduation from his anonymous account @kestrelknows, posting another eerily accurate prediction about a fire drill. Establishes his isolation, wit, and the ticking clock. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as superiority.

chapters.title: The Nemesis Clause
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Ms. Okonkwo pairs him with Tamsin Vale for a semester-long project on the school's failing robotics team. They argue in front of the class; she calls him 'the anonymous coward' under her breath. Beat: reluctant collision.

chapters.title: Tamsin's Ledger
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. We learn her scholarship depends on a state championship and her family can't know how bad things are. She keeps a literal ledger of debts and favors. Beat: pressure hidden behind competence.

chapters.title: Room B-4 Smells Like Solder
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. First visit to the abandoned robotics lab: dust, a half-built robot named MARGINALIA, and three leftover members — Priya, Dev, and quiet Jun — who greet Tamsin like family. Beat: unwanted warmth.

chapters.title: Tryouts Nobody Signed Up For
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. To keep funding, the team must field six members by Friday. Tamsin posts tryout flyers; Kestrel mocks them online anonymously. Two unlikely freshmen show up anyway. Beat: fragile hope.

chapters.title: The Account Problem
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Tamsin corners him with printed screenshots proving @kestrelknows predicted events only someone inside could know. He denies it badly. Beat: first crack in the armor.

chapters.title: Truce Terms
chapters.summary: Dual POV alternating scenes. They negotiate: she won't expose the account if he actually helps win regionals; he won't reveal her scholarship crisis. A handshake neither trusts. Beat: armed peace.

chapters.title: MARGINALIA Wakes Up
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Rewriting the robot's code overnight, Kestrel accidentally makes it respond to voice — badly, hilariously. The team laughs together for the first time. Beat: belonging sneaks past defenses.

chapters.title: Dev's Secret
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Dev is hiding that his family might move mid-season; Priya covers for him. Tamsin realizes everyone on this team is holding something up alone. Beat: empathy through leadership.

chapters.title: The Audition Letter
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The Halcyon Coding Academy sends Kestrel a final-audition invitation — a live build challenge the same weekend as the championship. He tells no one. Beat: dread beneath ambition.

chapters.title: Practice Makes Enemies
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Rival captain Sloane Whitaker taunts Tamsin at practice scrimmage; Kestrel defends her without thinking. Both are startled by it. Beat: alliance turning instinctive.

chapters.title: Two A.M. Debugging
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Alone in the lab at 2 a.m., Kestrel finds Tamsin already there, crying quietly over the ledger. They don't discuss it; they just work. Beat: intimacy without confession.

chapters.title: The Freshmen Gambit
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The two freshmen turn out to have unexpected talent — one is a mechanical prodigy. The roster fills to six. Beat: found family assembling itself.

chapters.title: Sloane's Offer
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Sloane privately offers Kestrel a spot on the elite team plus Halcyon connections if he sabotages Tamsin's code. He doesn't say no fast enough. Beat: temptation and shame.

chapters.title: Regional Qualifiers
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The team scrapes into regionals on a buzzer-beater fix Kestrel writes live. Celebration pizza; Tamsin falls asleep on Kestrel's shoulder. Beat: victory as glue.

chapters.title: What the Account Knows Now
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel posts something kind about the robotics team anonymously — then panics realizing Tamsin will recognize the phrasing. Beat: identity blurring between mask and man.

chapters.title: Jun Speaks
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Quiet Jun finally explains why he quit teams before: a coach humiliated him publicly. Tamsin promises this team is different — and means it. Beat: the cost of trust.

chapters.title: Halcyon Preview Day
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel visits Halcyon's campus; it's dazzling and cold, full of brilliant loners exactly like the self he's abandoning. Beat: the wrong dream looking perfect.

chapters.title: The Fight About Everything
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Tamsin discovers Kestrel met with Sloane (innocently, mostly) and explodes; he throws her secret ledger back at her. Both say unforgivable-adjacent things. Beat: midpoint rupture.

chapters.title: Week of Silence
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The team splits into camps; MARGINALIA sits untouched. Kestrel codes alone and hates how easy solitude still is. Beat: regression recognized.

chapters.title: Priya's Intervention
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Priya forces both leaders into the supply closet until they talk honestly — about fear, not strategy. They emerge not fixed, but willing. Beat: repair begins.

chapters.title: Apology in Code
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel can't say sorry aloud, so he fixes every bug in Tamsin's subsystems and leaves a comment: //for what it's worth. She reads it twice. Beat: apology in his native language.

chapters.title: State Bracket Announced
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The bracket drops: they'll face Sloane's team in the semifinal, and the final lands the same day as Kestrel's Halcyon audition. Tamsin learns about the conflict — and says nothing. Beat: sacrifice seeded.

chapters.title: The Anonymous Unmasking
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Sloane leaks @kestrelknows' identity schoolwide with doctored screenshots making Kestrel look cruel. The team goes cold; even the freshmen avoid him. Beat: public fall.

chapters.title: Nobody Defends Him
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin knows the screenshots are faked — she has the originals — but stays silent, furious he never trusted her first. Guilt compounds daily. Beat: silence as betrayal.

chapters.title: MARGINALIA, Abandoned
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel stops coming to the lab. The robot's voice module plays his old test phrase to an empty room. Beat: absence made audible.

chapters.title: What Tamsin Should Have Said
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Jun confronts Tamsin: 'You knew. Why didn't you say so?' She admits she wanted him to hurt a little. Beat: honesty with herself at last.

chapters.title: The Real Screenshots
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin publishes the unedited logs proving the account was observational, not malicious — and takes blame for her own silence. Beat: costly truth-telling.

chapters.title: Door Left Open
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel returns to find his lab stool kept, his name still on the roster, and a sticky note from each teammate. He doesn't cry where anyone can see. Mostly. Beat: forgiveness accepted.

chapters.title: Semifinal vs. Whitaker
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Against Sloane's polished machine, the misfits win on improvisation — MARGINALIA adapts mid-match using code Kestrel wrote as an apology. Beat: teamwork vindicated.

chapters.title: The Night Before Two Finales
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Tamsin secretly maps a route to get Kestrel to his audition and back for the final; Kestrel secretly decides to skip the audition entirely. Neither knows. Beat: converging sacrifices.

chapters.title: Championship Morning
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel leaves a note withdrawing from Halcyon and heads to the arena — but Tamsin intercepts him with the route plan, and the team physically escorts him to the audition instead. Beat: being chosen against your own self-sabotage.

chapters.title: The Audition
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Live build challenge: Kestrel abandons the safe solution and builds something collaborative in spirit — a program that improves when strangers contribute. The judges lean forward. Beat: authentic self wins.

chapters.title: The Final That Doesn't Matter
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Without Kestrel, the team fights the championship final and loses by a hair. Tamsin's scholarship hangs by a thread — but the team holds. Beat: losing what doesn't matter.

chapters.title: The Championship That Does
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Sprinting back from Halcyon with an acceptance call unanswered, Kestrel arrives to a defeated team and tells them the real result: he got in — and asked to defer a year. Beat: the true victory declared.

chapters.title: Ledger Balanced
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The principal, moved by the season and community support the team inspired, restores Tamsin's scholarship via a new mentorship fund. She crosses out the last debt. Beat: grace arriving undeserved and earned.

chapters.title: @kestrelknows Signs Off
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Final post from the anonymous account: a thank-you letter naming no one and everyone. He closes the laptop in the lab, surrounded by the team. Beat: mask retired willingly.

chapters.title: Graduation Countdown: Zero
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Graduation day. Kestrel walks with the team behind him; Tamsin hands him a new ledger page titled 'Things Owed: Nothing.' Beat: sentence served, sentence ended.

chapters.title: Deferred, Not Denied
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Summer begins: Kestrel formally defers Halcyon to stay through senior year leading the team, teaching freshmen, keeping MARGINALIA humming. Beat: choosing presence over escape.

chapters.title: Epilogue: Tryouts Next Fall
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, closing scene. New flyers go up: TRYOUTS — NO EXPERIENCE NEEDED, ALL ARE WELCOME. Kestrel adds one line in code-comment style: //you belong here. Beat: belonging, now open-source.
